$comment: Evaluation corpus for wellposed's SEMANTIC (jev-on-jev) checks. Scored by eval/semantic-agreement.mjs, which makes one live jev call per item.
method: Seven generators, one per check, were given the defect in plain English and explicitly forbidden from reading semantic.mjs, so the cases could not be shaped by the wording of the grader they test. Each wrote 5 positives and 5 adversarial negatives - questions that superficially resemble the defect but are actually well-posed. A second agent then re-labelled every item blind: no intended label, no rationale, and not told how many were positive.
caveat: Generator and adjudicator agreed on 70/70. Read that as self-consistency, NOT as correctness: both are the same underlying model and share its priors, so agreement cannot detect a bias they hold in common. It does establish that the items are unambiguous to that model. The independent signal is jev itself, which is a different model - where jev disagrees with these labels, either could be wrong, and the disagreement list is the part worth reading.

items.intent: Assign an operational severity to an inbound enterprise incident so paging and SLA clocks are right.

state.report: SSO login returns 500 for all users since 08:10 UTC; local password login still works for the 6 admins
state.workaround: admins can issue temporary passwords manually, ~4 min per user

question.instructions: Rate the operational severity of this customer-reported incident.
criteria: Cosmetic: no functional impact, nothing to work around
Minor: a non-critical feature is degraded for some users and a documented self-serve workaround exists
Major: a core workflow is broken for many users and the only workaround is manual and slow
Critical: the product is unusable for every user on the account and no workaround exists

items.rationale: Each level names both blast radius and workaround, which looks like two dimensions, but the two co-vary as a single standard severity axis that rises cleanly from cosmetic to critical.

items.intent: Decide whether an AML alert is worth escalating to a SAR filing.

One mild anomaly with a plausible innocent explanation already on file
Several anomalies that reinforce each other and have no documented explanation
A pattern matching a documented structuring typology with no legitimate business explanation

items.rationale: The levels are long and multi-clause, but every clause serves one axis — strength of evidence — and that strength rises monotonically from none to typology-matching.

items.intent: Rate redlined clauses in a vendor MSA so counsel knows which ones to fight over.

Neutral: standard mutual terms, no edits needed
Favorable: shifts more risk to the vendor than market standard

items.rationale: The scale crosses from harm to benefit, which can look like two opposed dimensions, but favorability is one bipolar axis and the levels ascend along it without a break.

items.intent: Assign an ED triage acuity level from the walk-in intake note.

items.intent: Decide whether an auto-refund macro may fire on a support ticket without an agent.
items.state: Ticket #48120 — order delivered 3 days ago. Customer: 'box showed up already opened and two of the four mugs are gone.' Refund requested: $38.99. Order history: no prior refunds, no chargeback on file, first contact on this order, single message in thread.

question.instructions: Should this ticket be held back from the automatic refund flow?

criteria.true: Something in the thread makes the automatic refund wrong to send right now — an open chargeback, a refund already issued on this order, or an amount above the $75 macro ceiling.
criteria.false: Nothing in the thread blocks it; the macro can send the refund as written.

items.rationale: The descriptions never repeat the phrase 'held back' and instead enumerate blockers, which reads at a glance like a different question, but 'a blocker exists' is exactly the yes case and 'no blocker' exactly the no case.

items.intent: Classify a return request into a reason category that drives downstream routing.
items.state: Return message: 'Ordered the walnut cutting board 18x12; what arrived is the bamboo one and it's a different size. Box was fine, item isn't damaged, it's just not what I picked.' Order line: WB-1812-WAL. Photo shows BB-1410-BAM.

question.instructions: Which return-reason category best fits this customer's message?

criteria.wrong_item_sent: A different SKU than the one ordered arrived; these go to the fulfillment audit queue.
criteria.damaged_in_transit: The correct item arrived broken, crushed, or leaking; these go to the carrier claims queue.
criteria.sizing_issue: The correct item arrived intact but does not fit; these go to standard returns.
criteria.changed_mind: No defect or error stated, the customer simply no longer wants it; standard returns with a restocking fee.

items.rationale: Each description trails a routing consequence, which can look like it describes something other than the reason, but every description leads with the defining condition for that category.

items.intent: Grade how well an NDA's assignment terms support survival through the counterparty's acquisition.
items.state: Mutual NDA (2024); counterparty is in acquisition talks. §9.2: 'Neither party may assign this Agreement without the other's prior written consent, except that either party may assign to a successor in a merger or sale of substantially all assets upon written notice.' No change-of-control termination clause appears elsewhere.

question.instructions: Rate how well this NDA's assignment terms support the agreement surviving the counterparty's acquisition, weakest support first.
criteria: The agreement terminates automatically on a change of control.
Assignment is barred outright, with no successor carve-out.
Assignment requires our prior written consent, with no deemed-consent provision.
Assignment to a successor in a merger is permitted on written notice to us.
The agreement expressly binds successors and assigns, change of control included.

items.rationale: No level uses a strength word, so the scale looks like it describes clause text rather than the asked-about strength, but the clause facts are ordered exactly weakest-to-strongest support as the instructions state.

items.intent: Decide whether a flaky CI test can be quarantined until someone fixes it.

state.suspect: seeds two promos in the same second; ordering by created_at is nondeterministic
state.other_coverage: promo stacking also covered by test_promo_stack_integration

question.instructions: Can this test be quarantined (skipped in CI) until someone fixes it?

criteria.true: The failures are not tied to a code change, and nothing on a payment or auth path loses its only coverage if this test stops running.
criteria.false: The failures track a real regression, or this is the only test covering a payment or auth path.

items.rationale: The 'true' description is written entirely in negations ('are not tied', 'nothing loses'), which superficially reads like an inverted answer, but it states the conditions under which quarantining is in fact safe.

items.intent: Triage urgency of a first-notice-of-loss report so the adjuster queue is ordered correctly.
items.state: FNOL notes: kitchen fire 2026-09-20 22:40, fire department on scene, no injuries reported. Family staying with relatives tonight; policy carries $2k/mo additional living expense. Home has no power and the back door was forced by responders and left unsecured. Policyholder is asking about a hotel.

question.instructions: Rate the urgency of this loss report, least urgent first.
criteria: Documentation only — no coverage decision needed this week
Routine — adjuster contact within 2 business days
Elevated — adjuster contact within 8 business hours; property unsecured or rental/lodging pending
Emergency — contact within 1 hour; home uninhabitable or someone was injured

items.rationale: The levels are phrased as contact deadlines rather than urgency adjectives, which a careless grader may read as measuring SLA instead of urgency, but the deadlines are the operational definition of urgency and run least to most as instructed.
